title: Cheap jobs, the Pelican job and Walter Pichon's lessons
summary: He played cheap jobs, took a banjoist's offered job at the Pelican where steamer musicians jammed, and learned music from Walter Pichon.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: Well I bet you wanted to be a musician at that time. Yeah.

Then I began to play a little cheap jobs for a dollar and a half. And what you could drink was just fun to me. The money didn't mean anything. I mean we just loved to play you know. And I'd get a drum and piano and my singing helped me out a whole lot. So I still was bumming with this little guy at Boynton San Diego. And he was a fellow, he didn't like to play for money. He liked to play for pleasure. And he had a little job at the Pelican N.A.s. And he quit the job. And I had sit in with them a couple of times. And they had a banjo player. We used to call him Van. His name is Joe. And he begged me to take the job. He said I could play enough and he would help me. So he persuaded me and I took the job. I was so nervous. But every day he would show me how to build certain cards and different things like that. And I was so much interested and I called on right away. And I had the pleasure of playing on this job. The steamer, all the fellows off the steamer capital used to come and jam. And I would just sit down and call. I couldn't play that much. I just could call. And I would call maybe one number for our. We had all the greatest musicians in the South playing down there. Sun Johnson and Taft off the boat and Eugene Porter and oh just a lot of great musicians that now have made a big name for themselves. And I stood on this job for oh maybe a year or something. And after I got off that job I think I knew every chord that they were playing at that time. So I got interested in it. My brother thought that I was interested in it. Then he began to explain to me a little about music. At this time my brother was playing with Walter Pichon's band. And I became good friends with Walter and Walter used to teach me.
Was he working on the boat those days or right at the top?

That was before he worked on the boat. And of course right after that they got a job on the boat. And well I learned a little bit about music. It's enough to take a piece in practice and play you know. Which made me get along pretty well. And then Sam Morgan died and his brother Isaiah kind of took over a band and made the trips that he used to make. He used to play all over the south.
